clue.text: G. M. Hopkins offers solace with a peal of bells, we hear

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'G. M. Hopkins offers solace with a peal of bells, we hear (6,7)', is the 1-down clue repeated; the real clue for this Bach work is missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: G. M. Hopkins offers solace with a peal of bells, we hear

clue.text: G. M. Hopkins offers solace with a peal of bells, we hear

indicators.note: the listener is told the bell-peal word is only heard, so its sound stands in for a near-identical spelling

parts.note: a carillon is a set of tuned bells, or the peal played on them
solace and comfort are synonyms

explanation.surface: The Victorian Jesuit poet consoles his readers to the sound of church bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns CARILLON (a peal of bells) into its sound-alike CARRION. One of Hopkins's 'terrible sonnets' opens 'Not, I'll not, carrion comfort, Despair'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a famous sonnet by Gerard Manley Hopkins, so it is something the poet offers.

clue.text: Reportedly sincere coinage

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for sincere is used for its sound only

parts.note: frank means sincere, open and honest

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be genuinely candid about money.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and is still the currency of Switzerland, a piece of coinage.

clue.text: Filled was her heart with inexpressible sweetness

definitions.text: Filled was her heart with inexpressible sweetness

parts.words: Filled was her heart with inexpressible sweetness
parts.note: a line from Longfellow's long poem about an Acadian girl parted from her lover; the 'her' is the heroine who gives the poem its title

explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's narrative poem is named after its heroine, the woman whose heart this line describes.

clue.text: Did Joseph Heller write twenty-one more of these?

definitions.text: Did Joseph Heller write twenty-one more of these?

parts.words: Did Joseph Heller write twenty-one more of these?
parts.note: Heller's novel is numbered 22, so the question imagines twenty-one earlier ones of the same kind

explanation.definitionFit: Heller's war novel is Catch-22, implying a series of twenty-two such snags.

clue.text: Associated by Mailer with The Dead?

definitions.text: Associated by Mailer with The Dead?

parts.words: Associated by Mailer with The Dead?
parts.note: Norman Mailer's war novel is called The Naked and the Dead, pairing the dead with the unclothed

explanation.definitionFit: People who go without clothes are the naked, the group Mailer's title puts beside the dead.

clue.text: Yesterday in Spain with English philosopher

definitions.meaning: A. J. ..., the logical positivist author of Language, Truth and Logic

explanation.surface: A Spanish memory of the day before shared with an English thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish uses this word for the day before today, and it is also the surname of the Oxford philosopher A. J. Ayer.

clue.text: "Blonde — rose up excited, / Moved to delight by the melody" (Auden)

definitions.text: "Blonde — rose up excited, / Moved to delight by the melody" (Auden)

parts.words: "Blonde — rose up excited, / Moved to delight by the melody" (Auden)
parts.note: lines from Auden's poem The Shield of Achilles era work describing the golden goddess of love rising up at the music

explanation.definitionFit: The golden-haired Greek goddess of love is the blonde figure in Auden's lines.

clue.text: Tennessee Williams's view of Franny, Zooey, Buddy and Seymour ?

definitions.text: Tennessee Williams's view of Franny, Zooey, Buddy and Seymour ?

parts.words: Tennessee Williams's view of Franny, Zooey, Buddy and Seymour ?
parts.note: Franny, Zooey, Buddy and Seymour are the Glass siblings of Salinger's stories, so a Williams play title is read as a collection of that family

explanation.definitionFit: Williams's play title, read literally, is a menagerie of Glasses, the Salinger family named in the clue.

clue.text: A predated rewrite is modified again

indicators.note: a rewrite reorders the material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An earlier-dated document, once rewritten, has been altered a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewrite' tells you to rearrange the nine letters of A PREDATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to modify, so something adapted a second time has been modified again.

clue.text: Miss Landon's Miss Churchill from Lambeth Elegy

indicators.note: the name is drawn out from the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A Victorian poetess's heroine emerges from an elegy written in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the name out of lambETH ELegy. Letitia Elizabeth Landon (L.E.L.) wrote the novel Ethel Churchill; Lambeth is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Landon's 1837 novel is titled after its heroine, so her first name identifies Miss Churchill.

clue.text: How Frederick Rolfe went, in short

definitions.text: How Frederick Rolfe went, in short

parts.words: How Frederick Rolfe went, in short
parts.note: Rolfe wrote under the pseudonym Baron Corvo, travelling under an assumed identity; 'in short' asks for the clipped form of the word

explanation.definitionFit: The clipped form of incognito means under a false name, as Rolfe lived when he styled himself Baron Corvo.

clue.text: After one more drink, Miss Parker would have been inferior to him

definitions.text: After one more drink, Miss Parker would have been inferior to him

parts.words: After one more drink, Miss Parker would have been inferior to him
parts.note: Dorothy Parker's quip: 'one more drink and I'll be under the ...', a play on 'under the table'

explanation.definitionFit: Parker's joke puts her beneath the man giving the party, the one whose drinks she has been drinking.

clue.text: White expedition leader

parts.note: Patrick White's novel follows a German explorer leading a doomed crossing of the Australian interior

explanation.definitionFit: Patrick White's 1957 novel is named after its explorer hero, who leads the expedition.

clue.text: A mere pub from Miss Brookner

definitions.text: A mere pub from Miss Brookner

parts.words: A mere pub from Miss Brookner
parts.note: Anita Brookner's Booker-winning novel is named after a Swiss lakeside hotel, which 'a mere pub' belittles

explanation.definitionFit: Brookner's novel takes its title from a hotel by a lake, a 'mere' being a lake as well as 'only'.

clue.text: Kit in Dickensian small business

parts.note: Kit is the loyal shop-boy in The Old Curiosity Shop, the small business of the title

explanation.definitionFit: Kit's surname in The Old Curiosity Shop identifies the boy who works in that little shop.

clue.text: Ark viable (after renovations) for composer

indicators.note: renovating rebuilds something, so the letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Noah's vessel is seaworthy once it has been restored, all for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after renovations' rearranges ARK VIABLE. Mily Balakirev led the Russian group of composers known as 'The Five'.
explanation.definitionFit: Balakirev was a nineteenth-century Russian composer, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Theological doctrine from cosmist's letters

indicators.note: the doctrine is made out of the letters of the word, reshuffled

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A religious teaching is extracted from the writing of a believer in cosmic philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from ... letters' asks you to rebuild COSMIST in a new order. Scotism is the teaching of the medieval philosopher Duns Scotus.
explanation.definitionFit: The system of Duns Scotus is a body of theological doctrine.

clue.text: Mad paladin of Ariosto

parts.note: Ariosto's epic ... Furioso is about a knight of Charlemagne who goes mad with love

explanation.definitionFit: Ariosto's furious hero is the Italian form of Roland, one of Charlemagne's twelve paladins.

clue.text: Mysterious feature of Edwin Drood and Weir of Hermiston

definitions.text: Mysterious feature of Edwin Drood and Weir of Hermiston

parts.words: Mysterious feature of Edwin Drood and Weir of Hermiston
parts.note: Dickens and Stevenson both died before finishing these novels, so neither has a conclusion

explanation.definitionFit: A story left without a conclusion is unresolved, as both novels were left when their authors died.

clue.text: Ayesha used to be a poor distillation

parts.note: Ayesha is the immortal queen of Rider Haggard's novel She
'has been' means used to be, so been stands for it

explanation.surface: A heroine reflects that she was once a weak spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayesha is 'She-who-must-be-obeyed' in Haggard's novel. A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, especially in Ireland, where rough illicit liquor is sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an illicit drinking place, home of cheap home-distilled liquor such as poteen.

clue.text: Consolations to be found, thought Wordsworth, "within the sonnet's scanty plot of ground "

definitions.text: Consolations to be found, thought Wordsworth, "within the sonnet's scanty plot of ground "

parts.words: Consolations to be found, thought Wordsworth, "within the sonnet's scanty plot of ground "
parts.note: Wordsworth's 'Nuns fret not' says those who feel too much liberty may find brief comfort in the narrow sonnet form

explanation.definitionFit: Comforts and consolations are synonyms, and Wordsworth's sonnet speaks of finding 'brief solace there'.

clue.text: Orson Welles filmed F for this counterfeit

definitions.text: Orson Welles filmed F for this counterfeit

parts.words: Orson Welles filmed F for this counterfeit
parts.note: Welles's 1973 documentary about forgery is titled F for ..., the missing word meaning a sham

explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeit is a sham or forgery, the subject and title word of Welles's film.

clue.text: Iris Murdoch's sank without trace

parts.note: in Murdoch's novel the great abbey ... lies sunk in the lake, and the new one falls in too

explanation.definitionFit: Murdoch's novel takes its title from the abbey's chiming instrument that ends up at the bottom of the lake.

clue.text: Doctor gets sentimentality returned from Burgess hooligan

indicators.note: something returned comes back the other way, so the word for sentimentality is read backwards

parts.note: goo is slang for gushing sentimentality

explanation.surface: A physician has mawkishness thrown back at him by a thug from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns GOO into OOG. In A Clockwork Orange, Anthony Burgess calls Alex's gang members droogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgess's invented slang word, from Russian for 'friend', names a member of a violent teenage gang.

clue.text: Lancet arch to present on ring

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
to present means to give

explanation.surface: A pointed Gothic window is offered with a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts the O on top of GIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogive is a pointed arch of the kind found in lancet windows in Gothic architecture.

clue.text: Aspersion started some literary upheavals recently

indicators.note: the starting letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: A smear began a few recent literary scandals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' takes the first letters of Some Literary Upheavals Recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a damaging insinuation against someone's reputation.

clue.text: A lovely woman in a spot! (Leigh Hunt)

definitions.text: A lovely woman in a spot! (Leigh Hunt)

parts.words: A lovely woman in a spot! (Leigh Hunt)
parts.note: Leigh Hunt's line pictures a fine woman in a country setting; the missing word describes that countryside spot

explanation.definitionFit: A rural spot is one in the countryside, the setting Leigh Hunt places his lovely woman in.

clue.text: Strange device for packing material

definitions.meaning: Longfellow's youth bears 'a banner with the strange device' bearing a Latin motto meaning 'higher'
wood shavings used as packing in crates

explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's banner motto is the Latin word for 'higher'; in America the same word is a trade name for fine wood shavings used in packing.

clue.text: Secretive odes might turn out to be polished poetry

indicators.note: the letters could turn out as something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Lyrics written in private could prove to be elegant verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might turn out to be' rearranges SECRETIVE ODES. Vers de société is light, witty, urbane verse on social themes.
explanation.definitionFit: This French term names light, elegant verse about polite society, refined and polished in style.
